newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sugar crop seen a tad lower in 96-97 cycle.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sugar crop seen a tad lower in 96-97 cycle.

text.p: Mexico's 1996-1997 sugar harvest is seen ending at 4.364 million tonnes, down from the record output of 4.377 million tonnes produced in 1995-1996, the National Sugar Chamber said Tuesday.
"We are estimating production to close the upcoming harvest at 4.364 million tonnes," spokesman Francisco Sanchez de Cima told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Mexico's annual sugar cycle runs traditionally from November to June.

He added the chamber, which is the umbrella organization for Mexico's 61 active sugar mills, estimated outout would dip a touch because of adverse weather conditions. Veracruz, Mexico's top sugar producing state, has been deluged with rain in recent weeks.
"Our estimation is lower than others," Sanchez added, refering to the government's Agroindustry Sugar Committee and the National Sugar Cane Growers Association.

Sanchez added the estimates were that an approximate total of 600,000 hectares had been sown with cane for this campaign. He said the forecast compared to the chamber's last cycle pre-crop estimate of 4.441 million tonnes.

Sanchez said the upcoming cycle would begin November 13 with the programmed start-up of the Atencingo sugar mill in the state of Mexico, which belongs to Mexico's largest sugar industrialists Grupo Escorpion.
